XX Открытый всеобщий синхронный чемпионат

XX Global Open Synchronous Championship

Season 2022–2023

Leg V (16 – 26.12.2022)



Notes for the reader:

 

Please familiarize yourself with the question pack before the game.

 

Words in caps (e.g., X, FIRST, IT, DO THIS) should be emphasized when reading out loud. After reading the answer, you should also read out other accepted answers and the commentary to the question. Reading out the name(s) of the author(s) is advisable but not necessary.

 

Additional notes for the reader are placed in square brackets before some of the questions. You must not read them out loud.

 

Phonetic transcriptions of selected words (in square brackets) are put within the text of some questions for the reader’s convenience.

 

Handouts for questions 11 and 35 are placed before the text of the questions. Please give the teams some time to familiarise themselves with the handouts, but do not read them out loud.

 

Good luck!





Edited by Maxim Merzliakov [mers-lyah-KOFF]



For testing the questions and for valuable remarks, the editor would like to thank the following individuals: Vladimir Broyda [BROY-duh], Daria Zhylkybayeva [zhil-key-BYE-eh-vuh], Anastasia Kalinina [kah-LEE-nee-nuh], Dmitri Karyakin [car-RYAH-kin], Alexander Korobeynikov [core-oh-BEY-nick-off] Alexander Kruglov [kroog-LOFF], Sergey Krupnik [KROOP-nick], Alexander Pechony [peh-CHOH-ny], Dmitri Ponomaryov [puh-no-mar-YOFF], Katerina Ryzhkova [rish-CAW-vuh], Timur Saifullin [sye-FULL-in], Anton Tilipman [til-lip-MAHN], Nail Farukshin [far-ROOK-shin], Valery Yudachov [you-dah-CHOFF].



Round 1



Question 1.

Mina Owczyńska [off-CHIN-ska], mother of Romain Gary, believed her son was a genius writer and begged him never to take part in THIS. Identify THIS using one word of Medieval Latin origin.

Answer: Duel(s).

Comment: Gary’s mother was born in the Russian Empire and believed that her son was equal in talent to Pushkin and Lermontov, and so she begged him never to fight in a duel, to avoid dying in the bloom of his literary career as they did.

Sources:

1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romain_Gary

2. Р. Гари. Обещание на заре (Romain Gary, La Promesse de l'aube); https://tinyurl.com/2hjf36ey

3. https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/duel#Etymology

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 2.

Handout:



(img 2022-2023_V_en_001.png)

Steven Pinker compared the attempts to teach apes human language to trying to force the animal on the picture to pick things up with its nostrils. These attempts were guided solely by the fact that its closest living relative is WHO?

Answer: Elephant(s) [also accept Proboscidea(ns)].

Comment: Two feet in length and looking like a guinea pig, the hyrax is the species closest related to elephants. Pinker compares language to the elephant’s trunk, another unique development that has no equivalent in any other extant animal. Pinker says that if researchers were as fixated on trunks as they are on language, they would conclude that the hyrax has one, just because it has nostrils.

Sources:

1. https://tinyurl.com/yc73d95j

2. С. Пинкер. Язык как инстинкт (Steven Pinker, The Language Instinct); https://tinyurl.com/4mstc8s6

3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyrax

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 3.

The Russian word for “arsenic” is linked not to bats, but to rodents. Nevertheless, in folklore the mineral arsenopyrite was described as a magic amulet, because it produces THIS when struck. Identify THIS.

Answer: The smell of garlic [accept any answer that mentions smell and garlic].

Comment: Because of its garlic smell, arsenopyrite was believed to be a magic amulet warding off undead, such as vampires, who are commonly associated with bats in legends. In fact, the mineral can keep away or poison rodents as well as bats, hence the Russian name.

Sources:

1. https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Мышьяк

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenopyrite

3. https://tinyurl.com/3jrk6kmf

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 4.

In the human body, THEY suppress the activity of platelets, while in another animal host, conversely, they block the production of an anti-coagulant. Both effects improve the probability of THEIR spread. Identify THEM.

Answer: malaria parasite(s) [accept plasmodium/a, malaria germ]

Comment: Platelets are responsible for blood clotting, and the malaria parasite affects them to facilitate feeding for blood-sucking mosquitoes who will then transmit the disease to new hosts. In the mosquito's body the parasite’s action is reverse: it blocks the production of a blood-thinning enzyme. The mosquito becomes more thirsty and bites more humans, increasing the probability of the parasite spreading. Parasites are very ingenious.

Source: К. Циммер. Паразит — царь природы (Carl Zimmer, Parasite Rex); https://tinyurl.com/2cdx4baf

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 5.

British scientist John Haldane would often accompany his father to a mine, and once narrowly escaped death in a methane bubble. Later he acquired a habit that made his friends afraid of standing close to him. Using another person remembered by the writer Bill Mesler in a story about Haldane’s habit, identify Haldane’s day and month of birth.

Answer: 5 November.

Comment: Haldane was a pyromaniac; for example, he liked keeping match and explosives in one pocket. His friends regarded this with fear and suspicion. We do not know what triggered his pyromania, whether it was that traumatic childhood experience with methane, or his birthday falling on the day Guy Fawkes attempted to burn down the English Parliament. The word “remembered” in the question hints at the song “Remember, remember the fifth of November!”

Sources:

1. Б. Меслер, Д. Кливз. Краткая история сотворения мира (Bill Mesler and H. James Cleaves II, A Brief History of Creation); https://tinyurl.com/yrwe3tpy

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._B._S._Haldane

3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Fawkes

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 6.

Evgeny Golovin [yev-GAY-ny go-law-VIN] writes that the saying “What a woman wants, God wants” is the inversion of a Latin quote from THIS. THIS is also the title of a death metal album. Identify THIS.

Answer: Malleus Maleficarum [accept Hammer of the Witches]

Comment: Golovin believes that this saying inverts the original “Feminum luxus, diabolum luxus”, meaning “A woman’s joy is the devil’s joy”, originally a quote from the 15th-century misogynistic treatise Hammer of the Witches. The book was an instruction on identifying and prosecuting witches. Its subject lies close to the interests of death metal bands; for example, its title became the title of an album by Pestilence.

Sources:

1. Е. Головин. Сентиментальное бешенство рок-н-ролла; https://tinyurl.com/yc8dyttt

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malleus_Maleficarum

3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malleus_Maleficarum_(album)

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 7.

To conceal his identity, a character in a historical mystery novel from the Brother Cadfael series assumes the name Matthew. Interestingly, by the end of novel some unexpected family relations are revealed. What was his real name?

Answer: Luke [accept Lucas].

Comment: The character, baptised after Luke the Evangelist, found no better trick than to assume the name of another Evangelist, Matthew. Interestingly, in the finale Cadfael admits that he is another character’s father, although not Luke’s, otherwise the parallel to Star Wars would have been too striking.

Sources:

1. Э. Питерс. Роковой обет (Ellis Peters, The Pilgrim of Hate); https://tinyurl.com/y75dnsw6

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Empire_Strikes_Back

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 8.

Brother Cadfael left the secular world to become a monk, but he still had deep affection for a certain Winifred, who he called “Girl”. What word was omitted in the previous sentence?

Answer: The.

Comment: This detail is likely an allusion to Sherlock Holmes, for whom “The Woman” was Irene Adler. However, in accordance with his era, Cadfael’s “The Girl” is a Welsh holy martyr, whose bones he helped to unearth and then was filled with love for her.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadfael

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 9.

A certain musical by Jonathan Larson is largely autobiographical. Its main female character dies of AIDS. The first production of this musical took place in 1996, exactly 100 years after THIS. Identify THIS.

Answer: the premiere of La Boheme [accept all answers that mention La Boheme or its first production specifically, without any wrong additions].

Comment: The musical Rent is based on the plot of La Boheme by Puccini. The setting is not Paris, but New York, though no less bohemian, and the characters are bohemian too. The main character dies not of tuberculosis, like in Puccini, but of AIDS, more relevant in the 20th century. The musical premiered exactly 100 years after the first production of the opera.

Sources:

1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rent_(musical)

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_boh%C3%A8me

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 10. [Note to the reader: do not indicate the italics. If you are showing the question text on a screen, remove the formatting beforehand.]



In a story by Maurice Druon, the Muses, listening to Apollo’s music, heard doves cooing, girls laughing in the fields, the sound of a flail threshing corn, and the wind’s plaintive cries in the reeds. Later Apollo claims to have played THEM. According to one suggestion, THEY were created under the impression made by rural areas around Mantua, where a certain person spent several years. Identify this person.

Answer: (Antonio) Vivaldi.

Comment: In Druon’s rendition of the myth about the contest between Apollo and Marsius, Aopplo’s music includes sounds belonging to all four seasons. According to one scholarly suggestion, Vivaldi’s Four Seasons concerti were written while he was living and working in Mantua.

Sources:

1. М. Дрюон. Дневники Зевса (Maurice Druon, Les Mémoires de Zeus); https://tinyurl.com/42u5s947

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Four_Seasons_(Vivaldi)

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 11.

The 1930 Soviet film Sleeping Beauty is set around a production of the eponymous ballet. It goes beyond the theatre scene, and some sequences in it symbolise how the art of ballet remains stagnant despite the illusion of progress. In a sequence filmed as a possible epilogue to the movie, THIS starts moving and gets away. Identify THIS exactly.

Answer: Apollo’s chariot.

Comment: The film shows the Bolshoi theatre both from within and from without, and the authors make an emphasis on the sculpture of Apollo’s chariot on its façade; it portrays movement, but always stays in place. In one of the epilogue scenes that ultimately didn’t make the cut, the sculptured horses seem to start moving, which symbolises the art awakening from slumber.

Sources:

1. https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Спящая_красавица_(фильм,_1930)

2. Д. Хитрова, Ю. Цивьян. Конец фильма; https://tinyurl.com/yhurmt8b

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 12.

Daria Khitrova [khit-RAW-va] writes that a film director may in some cases sacrifice its ending in order to adapt the product to different conditions. She compares the structure of a film to the anatomy of WHAT?

Answer: lizard.

Comment: Khitrova states that a film ending is like a lizard’s tail; in case of emergency it can be cast aside and a new and better one can be grown. Something similar happened to the ending of the Sleeping Beauty film from the preceding question.

Source: Д. Хитрова, Ю. Цивьян. Конец фильма; https://tinyurl.com/54fjzfsr

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov



Round 2.



Question 13.

A zybka is a type of Russian hanging cradle. Even though it’s made to rock from side to side, an old peasant woman used the word zybka when reporting her visit to a big city. What did she call a zybka?

Answer: lift [accept elevator].

Comment: She seemed to have no other word to describe a thing that hangs on a chain and moves around. So when reminiscing about her visit to Leningrad, the old woman said that she took a ride in a zybka.

Source: И. Левонтина. О чём речь; https://tinyurl.com/3zens7e3

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 14.

Handout:

“…and again she betrayed him, and the Philistines bound him”



The word suspense is derived from the verb suspend in the physical sense of hanging. According to Gilles Deleuze, the art of suspense was mastered by the Austrian, whose quote about the biblical Samson is on the handout. Identify this Austrian.

Answer: (Leopold von Sacher-)Masoch.

Comment: In Masoch’s works, the submissive victim is always expecting new torment (but doesn’t mind it). Deleuze mentions suspense in both senses, because Masoch’s characters are literally bound, manacled, suspended and crucified. The handout has a quote from Venus in Furs, in which the narrator muses about Samson who also suffered because of the power-hungry Delilah.

Sources:

1. Leopold von Sacher-Masoch, Venus in Furs; https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/6852/pg6852-images.html

3. Ж. Делёз. Представление Захер-Мазоха (Gilles Deleuze, Présentation de Sacher-Masoch); https://tinyurl.com/58uj53u9

4. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopold_von_Sacher-Masoch

5. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_bondage

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 15.

Russian poet Vyacheslav Ivanov, who spent a long time in Italy, thought that his colleague Alexander Blok’s behaviour was not worthy of his talent. Ivanov dedicated to Blok a poem titled God in an X. In X, one could actually see gods and goddesses, including Venus. Identify what X is, as exactly as possible.

Answer: Lupanar (accept Roman brothel and other answers matching that sense).

Comment: Ivanov criticised Blok for his lecherous behaviour and dedicated his poem God in a Lupanar specifically to Blok. In lupanars, i.e., Roman brothels there were wall-paintings of gods and goddesses, including Venus, the goddess of love.

Sources:

1. https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Иванов,_Вячеслав_Иванович

2. В. Иванов. Бог в лупанарии; https://tinyurl.com/492xr8wd

3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lupanar

4. https://tinyurl.com/a6hsba58

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 16.

Carl Zimmer contrasts the artificially modified K12 strain of E. coli with its wild strains and compares K12 to THIS. The author of this question notes that this comparison would be even more appropriate if the strain had a slightly different name. Identify this proposed name and identify THIS using only one word.

Answer: K9, dog(s) [accept: K9, canine(s), or in reverse order].

Comment: The wild strains that are potentially dangerous for humans, are compared to wolves, while the “domesticated” modified K12 strain used in lab studies is compared to dogs. The author thinks that an appropriate name for the “tame” strain would be K9, with an even closer association to dogs.

Sources:

1. https://tinyurl.com/2yu3b7pw

2. К. Циммер. Микрокосм. E. coli и новая наука о жизни (Carl Zimmer, Microcosm: E. coli and the new science of life); https://tinyurl.com/276tm45y

3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K9

4. The author’s own opinion; https://tinyurl.com/5yxeyx9v

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 17.

The entrepreneur John Templeton was bitter about the fact that many ignored the spiritual pursuit that represents another way to progress. In a document published about five decades ago, it is specifically stipulated that the Templeton X should be larger than ANOTHER X. Identify ANOTHER X.

Answer: Nobel Prize.

Comment: The Templeton Prize has been awarded since 1972 for discoveries and advances in spiritual life, and the laureate can be of any religion or even an atheist. Through the years among the laureates were Mother Teresa and the Dalai Lama, but also, for example, the scientist Freeman Dyson. The prize charter specifically states that its size in money shall always be greater than that of the Nobel Prize.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Templeton_Prize

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 18.

A hundred years ago, professors half-jokingly complained that they would teach THIS theory on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, and THAT one on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays. Identify THIS and THAT with one word each.

Answer: particle, wave [accept in any order, also with “quantum” and “corpuscle” instead of “particle”].

Comment: The theory in question is the theory of light, which baffled scientists with its dual wave-particle nature. Physicists joked that they would teach the wave theory 3 days a week and the particle theory 3 other days.

Sources:

1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave%E2%80%93particle_duality

2. М. Кумар. Квант (Manjit Kumar. Quantum); https://tinyurl.com/5n6mh2dr

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 19.

Initially it was thought that a black hole can only consume matter and energy. But after the emergence of Hawking’s radiation hypothesis, physicists started going as far as to mention the black hole mass effect. In the previous sentence, certain words have been substituted. Restore them.

Answer: half-life.

Comment: Hawking suggested that black holes can degrade and lose mass this way. As an analogy to elementary particles, the idea of half-life emerged, which depends on the initial mass and the intensity of radiation. The substitution uses titles of videogame series, Half-Life and Mass Effect.

Sources:

1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawking_radiation

2. https://tinyurl.com/ytenwmvn

3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-life

4. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_Effect

5. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-Life_(video_game)

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 20.

In the beginning of a famous novel, the main character tries to stand up from a chair but sits back down immediately to avoid embarrassment. Later, when the situation becomes even more frightening, the character mentiones a “monstrous eraser”. Identify this novel.

Answer: Thinner.

Comment: The character’s trousers were about to fall from him, so he was forced to sit back down immediately. However, his troubles were only starting; later, realising he was losing weight drastically, he compared this to a monstrous eraser deleting his kilograms.

Source: С. Кинг. Худеющий (Stephen King, Thinner); https://tinyurl.com/2fj2b83p

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 21. [Note to the reader: do not indicate the presence of the quotation marks. If you are showing the question text on a screen, delete them beforehand.]



The creators of Serutan, a cellulose-based laxative, set it against its synthetic alternatives. In its marketing slogan, people were asked to do something to “serutan”. What were they asked to do?

Answer: read backwards [accept any answer that means the same, like “spell backwards, pronounce in reverse” etc.]

Comment: Serutan was positioned as a natural medicine, and its slogan was “Read it backwards”. When read this way, it becomes “Nature’s”.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serutan

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 22. [Note to the reader: do not indicate the italics. If you are showing the question text on a screen, remove the formatting beforehand.]



In a book by Pascal Boyer, there is a suggestion that a particular type of THIS can be caused by foods that potentially impede development. THIS is set in a town called Bouville which can be translated as Mudtown. Identify THIS.

Answer: Nausea.

Comment: In pregnancy, nausea and vomiting can be caused by ordinary foods. According to one hypothesis, this type of nausea is an evolutionary mechanism that protects the mother’s body from toxins that can impede fetal development. The prototype for the disgusting town of Bouville in Sartre’s novel Nausea was Le Havre, where the author taught philosophy.

Sources:

1. П. Буайе. Объясняя религию. Природа религиозного мышления (Pascal Boyer, Religion Explained: The Evolutionary Origins of Religious Thought); https://tinyurl.com/ysdnj5wh

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nausea_(novel)

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 23.

After an unethical experiment, the physician Roberts Bartolow got attacked by outraged colleagues. Which Latin-based adjective did Sam Keane use in his book to describe this reaction?

Answer: autoimmune.

Comment: An autoimmune reaction is an attack on one’s own body cells by one’s immune system. Keane compares the medical community to the immune system: it did everything to expel Bartolow from its ranks after an inhumane experiment on a patient’s brain.

Sources:

1. С. Кин. Дуэль нейрохирургов (Sam Keane, The Tale of the Dueling Neurosurgeons); https://tinyurl.com/er3axchk

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autoimmune_disease

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 24.

In this question, X and Y stand for specific words. According to the philosopher Hegel, a falling brick is deadly because of its speed, so if a human is killed by it, it is actually killed by X and Y. The compound word made of X and Y often precedes a noun that comes from Latin. Which noun is it?

Answer: continuum.

Comment: X and Y stood here for “space” and “time”. Hegel’s idea was that it’s not the brick itself that is deadly, but rather the energy it acquires due to travelling in space and time. The combined notion of spacetime is also specifically called “spacetime continuum”. And we will continue our game after a break.

Sources:

1. Г. Гегель. Энциклопедия философских наук (Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel, Enzyklopädie der philosophischen Wissenschaften); https://tinyurl.com/y8s3h4yk

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacetime

3. https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/continuum#English

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov



Round 3.



Question 25. [Note to the reader: do not signal the italics. If you are showing the question text on a screen, remove the formatting beforehand.]



One character in Dickens’s Little Dorrit was seen as an economics genius but ended up bankrupting thousands. Bernard Shaw believed Little Dorrit impacts the reader more than THIS. In the USSR, Sergei Eisenstein was planning a screen adaptation of THIS, while German theatre directors made a play based on THIS. Identify THIS.

Answer: Capital [accept Das Kapital].

Comment: Shaw thought that Dickens’s novel is better at promoting revolutions and the downfall of capitalism than Capital by Karl Marx. Capital is not known for rigid research, and the author himself called it a literary work, so it makes sense to adapt it in theatre and film.

Sources:

1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Dorrit

2. https://tinyurl.com/2p8v93b9

3. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Das_Kapital

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 26.

John Greenleaf Whittier grew up in the early 19th century on a farm. As a child, he got a lot of free time to study poetry, because he could not help during harvest due to THIS. In many European languages, THIS is named after an older contemporary of Whittier. Who was that other person?



Answer: (John) Dalton.

Comment: Due to colour-blindness, Whittier could not distinguish ripe and unripe berries, the leisure time that he got was used for reading, and this helped him become a prominent poet. The condition was described in the late 18th century by John Dalton, using himself as a case study.

Sources:

1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Greenleaf_Whittier

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Dalton

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 27.

In the 13th century, at a festivity in the town of Treviso, girls were defending a “love castle” from boys. In one description we read that the girls fought with Xs, and the boys with Ys, and as a result they all got scratched. Identify X or Y, using only two words.

Answer: white rose [or “red rose”].

Comment: The girls’ weapons were white roses, symbols of chastity, and the boys had red ones, symbols of passion. This was another “War of the roses”, two hundred years before the English one.

Sources:

1.https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_the_Castle_of_Love

2. Е. Головин. Весёлая наука. Протоколы совещаний; https://tinyurl.com/4mcp5t3x

3. https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Война_Алой_и_Белой_розы

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 28.

Handout:



(img 2022-2023_V_en_001.jpeg)

Erich Maria Remarque was in love with the gracious and dangerous Marlene Dietrich. His nickname for her was X, but definitely not THIS KIND OF X. The recent movie called THIS KIND OF X is set in which country?

Answer: Wakanda.

Comment: Remarque called Marlene Dietrich a panther, but he could not have meant a black panther, because she was white and blonde. The 2018 movie Black Panther is set in the fictional country of Wakanda.

Sources:

1. https://tinyurl.com/3f38srz3

2. https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Чёрная_пантера_(фильм,_2018)

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 29.

In 1957, a postgraduate at the Leningrad Mining School was awarded for her exploration of the river Lena valley. Vasily Avchenko [AF-chen-caw] writes about her and mentions a certain song. A few years before that, Marni Nixon, a professional singer from USA, helped another person to sing this song. Who was that other person?

Answer: Marilyn Monroe [acceprt Norma Jean Baker]

Comment: In the 1950s, Larissa Popugaeva [poh-poo-GUY-eh-vah] discovered a diamond deposit in Yakutia. For this she received a government award, although her scheming colleagues took the credit for the discovery. Marilyn Monroe sang Diamonds Are a Girl’s Best Friend in the movie Some Like It Hot and was helped to reach the high notes by Marni Nixon, a renowned soprano.

Sources:

1. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larisa_Popugayeva

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zarnitsa_mine

3. https://tinyurl.com/2p864t9m

4. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lena_(river)

5. В. Авченко. Дальний Восток: иероглиф пространства. Уроки географии и демографии; https://tinyurl.com/mrxvk2yr

6. https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamonds_Are_a_Girl%E2%80%99s_Best_Friend

7. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marni_Nixon

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 30.

Nikolay Chernyshevski’s wife was a very progressive-minded woman. Vladimir Nabokov wrote about the many lodgers and guests of the Chernyshevskis and used a phrase that means literally “from A to Z”. A better known, but less detailed alternative to what he meant by this phrase, is based on THIS. Identify THIS using a word that originated in English.

Answer: Baseball.

Comment: Olga Chernyshevska surrounded herself with numerous admirers and lovers, with whom she was “in different stages of amorous intimacy”, according to Nabokov. For these “stages” he used the metaphor “from A to Z”. That implies many more stages than in the well-known baseball metaphor for intimacy.

Sources:

1. https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Чернышевская,_Ольга_Сократовна

2. В. Набоков. Дар (Vladimir Nabokov, The Gift); https://tinyurl.com/5bvntwfu

3. https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Русская_дореформенная_орфография

4. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball_metaphors_for_sex

5. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baseball

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 31.

John Olsson writes that THEIR telltale sign is that THEY are forced to use very rare synonyms. For example, THEY would describe a rich interior as lavish instead of luxury. Identify THEM, using a word of Latin origin.

Answer: Plagiarists.

Comment: Olsson’s book deals with linguistic text analysis, for example, finding evidence of plagiarism. He observes that plagiarists usually try to “copy with variations” and substitute individual words with synonyms. The original text would typically use the more common words for things, and so plagiarists are forced to use obscure words.

Sources:

1. Д. Олссон. Слово как улика (John Olsson, Forensic Linguistics); https://tinyurl.com/2pv9hcmr

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plagiarism

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 32.

To preserve secrecy, the Swedish Academy uses codenames for nominees to the Nobel Prize. The British writer Doris Lessing, once a member of the Communist party, got a two-word codename. Identify this codename.

Answer: Little Dorrit.

Comment: Her first name sounded like the Dickens character’s surname, and her surname had “less” in it. Moreover, she used to be a Communist, and you already know from our questions that this novel by Dickens has ideas that lie close to Communism.

Sources:

1. https://tinyurl.com/2p872brv

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doris_Lessing

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 33.

THEY first appeared in 1948, and at first they differed from the neighbours’ version only by an overprint. THEY feature a quote from Prophet Muhammad: “Seeking an honest livelihood is an act of worship”. Identify THEM using only two words.



Answer: Pakistani rupees.

Comment: Pakistani rupees were introduced soon after the country’s independence, but at first they were just Indian Rupees with “Government of Pakistan” overprinted on them. On some rupee notes, the translation of a Muslim hadith on money can be found.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistani_rupee

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 34.

During the conquest of Siberia, Russians faced stern resistance from the Chukchi [CHOOK-chi], a people from the far north. One of their customs had, among others, the function of intimidation. What designation, known since late 3rd century, can be explained by a similar custom?

Answer: Picts.

Comment: Chukchi face tattoos served, among others, the purpose of striking fear into their enemies. Russians even called them “paint-faces”. The Roman Empire, during its conquest of the British Isles, also faced tribes from the north that had that same custom. So Romans called these tribes picti – “the painted ones”. Both Picts and Chukchi resisted the invaders fiercely.

Sources:

1. https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Присоединение_Чукотки_к_России

2. https://tinyurl.com/6kj6mfpw

3. https://tinyurl.com/58bhdj3m

4. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Picts

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 35.

The bones of Aletopelta were found in California with shells attached to them. This led to the suggestion that after the animal died, its skeleton became the base for THIS. Which instance of THIS has the width of about 150 km?

Answer: The Great Barrier Reef.

Comment: THIS stands here for a reef. Bivalve mollusc shells attached to the dinosaur skeleton led to the suggestion that the dinosaur had once drowned in a river, and the carcass was then washed out to the sea and became part of a reef. The southern stretch of the Great Barrier Reef has the width of 152 km.

Sources:

1. https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aletopelta

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Barrier_Reef

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov

Question 36.

The book titled Norwegian Wood features Ruben Knutsen who builds a tidy stack of wood every year. The author of this question learned what then happens to the stack and compared it to THIS. Identify THIS, using a word in which all vowels are the same.

Answer: mandala.

Comment: The stacks that Knutsen builds are circular and resemble a mandala, the Buddhist symbol of the universe. For one specific ritual, a mandala is painstakingly created using coloured sand and then destroyed, reflecting the fleeting nature of the universe. Knutsen does the same, he builds a stack and destroys it.

Sources:

1. Л. Миттинг. Норвежский лес (Lars Mitting, Hel Ved); https://tinyurl.com/yzzhstkf

2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandala

3. An opinion by the author of this question; https://tinyurl.com/ye24nadb

Author: Maxim Merzlyakov
